name: Mount Everest
description: The highest mountain on Earth, Mount Everest stands as the ultimate mountaineering challenge. Located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas, it attracts hundreds of climbers each year despite its notorious death zone above 8,000 meters. The mountain is known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet.

name: K2
description: Known as the 'Savage Mountain,' K2 is widely regarded as the most dangerous and difficult mountain to climb. Its steep pyramidal shape and unpredictable weather create conditions far more treacherous than Everest. For every four climbers who have reached the summit, one has died trying.

name: Kangchenjunga
description: The third highest mountain in the world, Kangchenjunga is revered as sacred by the people of Sikkim and Darjeeling. By tradition, climbers stop just short of the actual summit out of respect for local beliefs. Its name translates to 'Five Treasures of the Great Snow,' referring to its five peaks.

name: Lhotse
description: Connected to Everest via the South Col, Lhotse is the fourth highest mountain on Earth. Its massive south face is one of the steepest walls in the Himalayas, rising 3.2 km in just 2.25 km of horizontal distance. Many Everest expeditions pass through Lhotse's flanks on the standard South Col route.

name: Makalu
description: The fifth highest mountain in the world, Makalu is an isolated peak shaped like a four-sided pyramid. Located 19 km southeast of Mount Everest, it is known for its striking beauty and steep, exposed ridges. The mountain has one of the lowest success rates among the 8,000-meter peaks.

name: Cho Oyu
firstAscentBy: Herbert Tichy, Joseph Jöchler & Pasang Dawa Lama
description: Considered the easiest of the 8,000-meter peaks, Cho Oyu is a popular choice for climbers preparing for Everest. Its name means 'Turquoise Goddess' in Tibetan. The northwest ridge route from Tibet offers a relatively straightforward path to the summit with minimal technical difficulty.

name: Dhaulagiri
description: Dhaulagiri, meaning 'Dazzling White Mountain,' held the title of world's tallest known peak for thirty years before Kangchenjunga was surveyed. Its enormous south face rises over 4,000 meters from the Kali Gandaki gorge, making it one of the greatest vertical reliefs on Earth. The mountain is known for fierce storms and avalanche-prone slopes.

name: Manaslu
description: Known as the 'Mountain of the Spirit,' Manaslu is the eighth highest peak in the world. It has become increasingly popular as an alternative to Everest, offering a challenging yet accessible 8,000-meter experience. The Manaslu Circuit trek around the mountain is one of Nepal's most spectacular trekking routes.

name: Nanga Parbat
description: Called the 'Killer Mountain,' Nanga Parbat earned its fearsome reputation from the numerous lives lost during early expeditions. Its Rupal Face is the tallest mountain face in the world at 4,600 meters. Hermann Buhl's solo first ascent without supplemental oxygen remains one of mountaineering's greatest feats.

name: Annapurna I
description: Annapurna was the first 8,000-meter peak ever climbed and remains the deadliest of them all. Its south face is considered one of the most challenging climbs in the world. The mountain is notorious for avalanches, and its fatality-to-summit ratio is the highest among the fourteen 8,000-meter peaks.

name: Denali
firstAscentBy: Hudson Stuck, Harry Karstens, Walter Harper & Robert Tatum
description: Denali is the highest peak in North America and one of the most prominent mountains on Earth. Its extreme cold, high latitude, and massive vertical rise from base to summit make it a formidable challenge. Climbers must contend with temperatures as low as -40°C and carry all their supplies on sleds across glaciers.

name: Kilimanjaro
description: Africa's highest peak is a dormant stratovolcano and the tallest freestanding mountain in the world. Kilimanjaro is unique among the great peaks as it requires no technical climbing skill, making it accessible to trekkers worldwide. Its glaciers are rapidly retreating due to climate change and may disappear entirely within decades.

name: Mont Blanc
description: The highest peak in the Alps and Western Europe, Mont Blanc is often called the birthplace of modern mountaineering. Its first ascent in 1786 is considered the beginning of alpinism as a sport. Despite being a non-technical climb by the standard route, it claims more lives per year than any other mountain due to the sheer number of attempts.

name: Matterhorn
description: With its iconic pyramidal shape, the Matterhorn is perhaps the most recognizable mountain in the world. The first ascent in 1865 ended in tragedy when four of the seven climbers died during the descent. Today, the Hörnli Ridge remains a classic alpine route that demands solid rock-climbing skills and a head for exposure.

name: Aconcagua
description: The highest peak in both the Western and Southern Hemispheres, Aconcagua is the tallest mountain outside of Asia. While not technically difficult by the Normal Route, its extreme altitude and fierce winds make it a serious undertaking. The mountain serves as an important stepping stone for climbers aspiring to tackle the Himalayan giants.

name: Mount Elbrus
description: The highest mountain in Europe, Elbrus is a dormant volcano with twin summits located in the Caucasus Mountains. Its relatively gentle slopes and cable car access make it one of the more accessible of the Seven Summits. However, sudden storms, whiteout conditions, and crevassed glaciers still claim several lives each year.
